title: Course Design and Teaching
answer: Curriculum mapping, assessment, personalised learning, tutors and lecture materials.

children.name: Curriculum and Learning Outcomes
children.blurb: Curriculum and learning outcomes in course design and teaching refer to the planned sequence of content, activities, and assessments that define what learners should know and be able to do by the end of a course or program.

children.name: Generating Assessments
children.blurb: Generating assessments covers the creation of quiz questions, test items, rubrics, distractors, feedback, and aligned learning outcomes from course materials.

children.name: Personalised Learning and Early Warning
children.blurb: Personalised learning and early warning covers AI systems that adapt instructional content, pace, and feedback to individual learners, and that flag students at risk of falling behind or dropping out.

children.name: Course-Specific AI Tutors
children.blurb: Course-specific AI tutors are software systems built or configured for a single course, using the course syllabus, readings, assignments, and instructor guidance to answer student questions and give feedback.

children.name: Lecture Materials from Notes
children.blurb: The topic covers turning an instructor's raw notes, outlines, or annotated readings into structured teaching artifacts such as slide decks, handouts, study guides, and lecture scripts.

sections.body: This field applies machine learning and language models to the practical work of designing and running courses. Right now AI is being used to draft learning objectives, generate quiz questions and rubrics, flag students who may be falling behind, answer subject questions in a tutor style, and turn lecture notes into slides or summaries. These are working tools in classrooms and universities, not just research prototypes. The systems operate on text, course materials, and student activity logs.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are fairly reliable, such as turning a set of notes into a first draft of slides or generating multiple choice questions from a textbook chapter. Other tasks remain uneven, especially personalised learning and early warning, where models can misread a student's struggle or overstate a risk. Honest limits include a lack of common sense about pedagogy, occasional factual errors in tutor answers, and the need for a teacher to review almost everything. The work is strongest as a drafting and triage aid, not as a replacement for an instructor's judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from planning to delivery. Curriculum and Learning Outcomes covers how AI helps map topics to goals and sequence a syllabus. Generating Assessments looks at quizzes, rubrics, and exam questions. Personalised Learning and Early Warning deals with adapting content and spotting students who need help. Course-Specific AI Tutors examines subject focused assistants that answer questions and give feedback. Lecture Materials from Notes shows how raw notes become slides, summaries, or study guides. A reader would start with curriculum, then move through assessment and personalisation, and finish with tutors and materials.
